messages:
liv: heads up — after the roles/perm refactor deployed in canary, a customer reported that Viewer accounts can no longer see Project Settings > API keys. repro on my end.

alex: can repro. backend returns 403 on GET /api/projects/:id/keys. payload: {error: "forbidden", detail: "missing view_api_keys"}. saw this start after deploy 2026-03-20T03:22Z.

sam: that makes sense — frontend gating checks `can_view_editor` which we removed as part of the role split. viewer used to implicitly map -> view secrets, now not. quick fix is to gate on explicit `view_api_keys` permission. will draft PR.

maria: quick triage: this blocks customers from retrieving their own API keys (availability + UX). not a data leak but definitely bad for onboarding. propose we treat as P2; if it affects paid accounts in prod, escalate. ensure audit logging of all 403s.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: detected increased 403 rate for endpoint /api/projects/*/keys in prod-canary cluster-3. Proposed action: hold rollout and patch canary.

liv: plan: 1) restore explicit `view_api_keys` to Viewer role in authz config as immediate patch, 2) update UI gating to check explicit permission (sam), 3) add an audit-log query to enumerate affected orgs and backfill role bindings where reviewers expect implicit access, 4) canary patch to 10% then full rollout. also add an incident annotation in the audit logs referencing the deploy id.

alex: I'll run a quick audit query: `SELECT org_id, count(*) FROM audit_logs WHERE endpoint LIKE '/api/projects/%/keys' AND status = 403 AND ts >= '2026-03-20' GROUP BY org_id;` will push results to #customer-impact once ready. Also will add a migration script to backfill `view_api_keys` for orgs that relied on the old mapping.

sam: PR opened: https://go/redwood/pr/1234 — backend patch + frontend gating + unit tests. includes test for `viewer` role getting view_api_keys=true.

maria: add KMS check as well — make sure key metadata (owner, created_at) still redacts for viewers even after we restore permission. we don't want to accidentally reveal key material.

cs-bot: cs-alert: flagged 3 accounts who attempted key access and failed since deploy. paging cs-team.

liv: thanks — I'll create a short runbook entry and add a postmortem skeleton. if anyone finds orgs where Viewer should not have this permission, flag them here before backfill.
